backbone: Induction on dimension and defining degrees via the ABPZ degeneration reduction, transporting the Virasoro equations (with Hodge-weighted contractions) through capped degeneration chains to complete intersections.
quote: used nodal invariants to reconstruct the full Gromov--Witten theory of complete intersections by induction on dimension and defining degrees

backbone: Chen's equivalence reduces bounded klt complements to a uniform lct threshold for birational contractions, proved by contradiction along a sequence using constrained normalized-volume minimization and valuations.
quote: We formulate it in Proposition~\ref{prop:birational-threshold} and prove it by contradiction.

backbone: Split by Picard number and pseudoindex; Kanemitsu handles rho>1, characterization theorems leave pseudoindex 4 and 5, excluded via minimal-curve characteristic-class constraints with an exact computer certificate.
quote: Standard characterization theorems leave pseudoindices four and five; the other possibilities are excluded or give projective space $\mathbb P^6$ and the smooth quadric $Q^6$.

backbone: DPS splitting of the universal cover; a torus-invariant anticanonical section on the remaining factor (finite-volume theorem by induction on dimension) times canonical frames descends, and its etale norm gives the section.
quote: Its product with those frames descends to a finite \'etale cover, and its finite \'etale norm then gives a section on \(X\).

backbone: Construct the equivalence from Whittaker coefficient and Poincare functors and prove J_s R_s -> Id is an isomorphism at irrational level by deforming the ordinary-level comparison and a conservative finite Whittaker test.
quote: We construct a comparison and prove that it is an isomorphism

backbone: Uniformize finite approximations (finite transfer), pass to normalized limits by compactness, and use transboundary extremal-length barriers and fused path laws to exclude noncircular limiting complementary components.
quote: The additional tasks here are to fuse the countable tests into one law controlling all boundary components, to preserve compatibility as tests are appended, and to exclude all possible noncircular limiting components.

backbone: Assume excess growth of inverse-square integral means; an eigenmeasure of a dyadic transfer operator gives an affine law on univalent maps forcing a Jacobian sign contradicted by saddle-maximum critical-point pairing.
quote: Our proof encodes hypothetical excess growth in a probability law on conformal maps. That law imposes an algebraic sign on an expected Jacobian; a geometric pairing of critical points imposes the opposite sign.

backbone: Prepare pair measures with angular cap bounds (radial projection gain, Orponen-Shmerkin incidence input), then bound Fourier shells of the distance measure by recursive profile reductions closed by a potential argument.
quote: We prove every reduction, including the support conditions needed for its iteration.

backbone: Reduce to a discrete multiplicity estimate; assume the critical exponent is positive, extract a differentiability point and a stationary equality configuration, then contradict it via entropy increments and projection constraints.
quote: Suppose otherwise. Choose an open interval \(I\) of \(p\)-values, with lower endpoint \(p_{\min}>2\), on which \(h(p,0)>0\).

backbone: Reduce a.e. convergence to a good-set integral bound for bounded-height inputs summed over layers; prove it by a finite dyadic procedure with budgets, stopping rules and entropy-compression refinements.
quote: For positive input, apply the finite procedure of \Cref{sec:procedure}, with the common stopping rule in the statement.

backbone: Build a balanced auxiliary trigonometric polynomial, sample it along quadratic waves of nearly constant modulus to get flat real coefficients in [-1,1], then round to signs by a discrepancy argument.
quote: The construction makes the normalized Fourier maximum close to one while keeping $N^{-1}\sum_k X_{N,k}^2$ close to one. The latter condition makes $\mu(X_N)/N$ small. A discrepancy argument then replaces the coefficients by signs

backbone: Combine the cited packet-propagation (elliptic capacity) and 3D Kakeya maximal theorems via density conversion to weighted tubes, sparse-ball epsilon removal, multiscale covers, then transfer to general surfaces.
quote: The remainder of the proof gives the density conversion, the estimates for rough \(L^3\) graph data, and the passage to general surfaces.

backbone: Assume excessive L3 growth, localize an extremal sequence and least-aspect saturated path, exclude the isotropic alternative (Loomis-Whitney, projections) and the matched-aspect alternative via rate transfer, reaching contradiction.
quote: To prove this bound, assume excessive growth and localize a sequence whose scores approach the largest possible rate.

backbone: Reduce to a cubic packet-mass functional per frequency annulus; assume its growth exponent exceeds the allowed loss, extract extremal cylinder configurations, and contradict via entropy inequalities plus Ren-Wang and wave-envelope inputs.
quote: The extremal reductions and entropy inequalities then connect this lower-dimensional information to the three-dimensional wave estimate.

backbone: Reduce to a short-time maximal estimate via endpoint square summation; prove a uniform dyadic packet distribution estimate by induction on scales using transverse power saving (by contradiction), sparse and bilinear estimates.
quote: We will obtain a broad bound with constant depending on $K$ and a narrow contraction with a constant independent of $K$. We then choose $K$, the base scale, and the induction constant in that order.

backbone: Prove relative excess decay at every scale by compactness (reflectionless limits, affine rigidity of normalized heights), propagate flatness along cube chains, pack failures (Carleson), then David-Semmes BWGL gives UR.
quote: Relative excess improvement at every scale

backbone: Prove a disjoint-annulus count estimate via a dimension-free matrix trace energy and Gaussian heat dissipation (energy increase telescopes over scales), then pass from counts to full r-variation.
quote: Each child has one parent and weight \(2^{2(k-1)}\), one quarter of the parent's weight, so these increases telescope.

backbone: Reduce to a restricted band estimate; time-frequency tile/tree decomposition with forest selection, iterating a strict constant-one finite Fourier inequality across an angular hierarchy so losses do not accumulate.
quote: An unspecified constant in this inequality would accumulate at every angular level and destroy the argument.

backbone: Probabilistic method: a random routed periodic set of small density hits every x+tq^n for t in [1,2] off a small repaired set; a summable union of dilations/reflections gives the complement.
quote: The proof below belongs to the probabilistic approach of Kolountzakis~\cite{Kolountzakis1997}.

backbone: Prove a signed finite-band gradient estimate via disk-moment cancellation and telescoping dyadic prices over scales, then extend to Sobolev inputs by localization and Lahti-Weigt to obtain the weak gradient bound.
quote: The masses paired at successive levels form a telescoping sum.

backbone: Reduce to uniform local-form constants C_N; using the Leng-Sah-Sawhney inverse theorem with curvature localization prove an absorption bound C_N <= A + cC_N, giving C_N bounded.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:completion} chooses the parameters and completes the absorption.

backbone: A conformal lens with uniform boundary law plus a holomorphic mass estimate at an isolated zero bounds an integral of feasible-simplex volumes, giving the volume-product bound; equality via a three-ball property.
quote: A holomorphic mass estimate turns that boundary law into a lower bound for an integral of feasible-simplex volumes over the primal body.

backbone: Variational representation with a continuous affine normalization, a spherical sign estimate from harmonic multipliers, and a strict inequality for norms yield a bilinear inequality whose equality case forces ellipsoids.
quote: Our proof uses the classical first-variation and spherical-transform frameworks, but requires estimates and an affine normalization that apply to arbitrary bodies.

backbone: Construct random families of label sets (cut measures) via multiscale updates on a column model of the planar graph: every outcome gives the upper bound, random local changes give the lower bound.
quote: The random construction chooses these entire families; the labels index their cuts. Every outcome has the required upper bound. Random local changes supply the lower bound.

backbone: Cohn-Kumar linear programming bound: construct sharp Gaussian Fourier minorants by interpolation with an exact finite certificate, then mix Gaussians via Bernstein-Widder for all completely monotone potentials.
quote: The proof constructs sharp Gaussian Fourier minorants using an atomic interpolation certificate.

backbone: Approximate polytopes by smooth weights; log-concavity of their integral reduces to a variance bound for sums of even powers of linear forms, proved in moment coordinates via a Bochner identity.
quote: Thus it suffices to prove that the integral of the smooth weight is log-concave when each $h_i$ varies geometrically.

backbone: Upper bound: random subset-sum sampler and weighted branching hierarchy of folded Gaussian blocks yield a lattice whose shear covers; lower bound: random symmetric body plus counting over finitely many periodic patterns.
quote: A second moment estimate alone gives a good approximation at most base points. A second group of random shifts upgrades this to a lower bound at \emph{every} base point.

backbone: Assume the optimal LSI constant exceeds the claim; take critical regularized extremal laws, derive a Gaussian prediction identity and nearly-first-eigenfunction hierarchy, then reach a contradiction via divergence of a scale integral.
quote: Covariance observations and the contradiction

backbone: Construct a distribution of bounded gradients matching weighted pth moments (convex separation, electrical-flow localization, Poisson sampling), then sample d independent copies; Hoeffding and a union bound give the embedding.
quote: For the value in~\eqref{eq:sampling-dimension} with $C$ sufficiently large, a union bound over $|E|<n^2/2$ edges is less than one.

backbone: Explicit determinant polynomial p_Q from a certified rank-20 Hankel seed; assuming a semidefinite lift, analytic Gram factors tested by a positive moment functional yield a contradiction.
quote: We construct a rank-twenty positive semidefinite Hankel matrix whose kernel has strong multiplication properties.

backbone: Assume the bound fails; take an optimal partition with fewest active cells, derive deletion and two-cell competition constraints on centroid radii, exclude five or more cells, with rational numerical enclosures.
quote: We argue by contradiction and henceforth assume \begin{equation}\label{ext:contradiction} C>B^2=\frac{9}{8\pi}. \end{equation} Choose an optimal partition with the fewest cells of positive measure
